notes: ReyDesk v2 identity test vectors. Source of truth: docs/REYDESK_V2_IDENTITY_REMOTE.md sections 1.2, 1.3, 1.6, 2.1-2.4, 3.2, 3.3, 3.9. Task T2.

Every value was computed by two independent implementations (Python stdlib with its own P-256 math and RFC 6979 signing; Node 24 using OpenSSL via node:crypto) and the outputs were deep-compared (0 differences) before this file was written.
TEST KEYS ONLY: private_scalar_hex values are published here on purpose. Never ship or trust them.
Hex is lowercase, no separators. Strings are UTF-8. 'empty' means a zero-length byte string.
LP(x) = 4-byte big-endian unsigned length of x, then x. Identical to PairingSignature.BuildReconnectPayload. A string field is its UTF-8 bytes.
Crockford base32 alphabet: 0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ (value = index). Bits are read most significant first; char i takes 5 bits.
SPKI = DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo of the P-256 key, uncompressed point, 91 bytes: 3059301306072a8648ce3d020106082a8648ce3d030107034200 || 04 || X(32) || Y(32).
Key fingerprint = SHA-256(SPKI), 32 bytes.

Key ID = top 60 bits of the fingerprint = (big-endian uint64 of fingerprint[0..7]) >> 4, as 12 Crockford chars. key_id_display = groups of 4 joined by '-'; the UI prefixes the label 'KEY ' (not part of the value). Key ID has no check char.
fingerprint_display = 256 fingerprint bits followed by 4 zero bits = 260 bits = 52 Crockford chars, 13 groups of 4 joined by one ASCII space.

Desk ID = 11 data chars (55 bits, data_bits_hex < 2^55, char 0 = top 5 bits) + 1 check char. check_value = (sum over i=0..10 of (i+1) * value(data[i])) mod 31; check_char = alphabet[check_value], so it is never 'Z'. display = 3 groups of 4 joined by '-'.

Desk ID parse, per input code point, in this order: (1) drop '-' U+002D, ' ' U+0020, and bidi controls U+200E U+200F U+2066 U+2067 U+2068 U+2069; (2) map Persian digits U+06F0-U+06F9 and Arabic-Indic digits U+0660-U+0669 to ASCII 0-9 (no other digit sets: do NOT use char.GetNumericValue, which accepts superscripts, fractions and fullwidth digits); (3) uppercase ASCII a-z only (no culture-sensitive ToUpper); (4) I and L -> 1, O -> 0, U dropped; (5) anything not in the alphabet -> BAD_CHAR. Then length != 12 -> BAD_LENGTH, then check char mismatch -> BAD_CHECK. Error precedence: BAD_CHAR, BAD_LENGTH, BAD_CHECK. canonical = the 12 uppercase chars without separators; this is the form stored, sent on the wire, signed and hashed.
Known limit (by design, spec 1.3): a 0 <-> Z substitution is not detected (value difference 31). The vector labelled 'undetectable' must parse as ok.

Remote code parse (RemoteCode.normalize): drop the same separators and bidi controls as Desk ID, map the same digit sets, anything else -> BAD_CHAR, then exactly 6 ASCII digits or BAD_LENGTH. Leading zeros are significant.
QR token = base64url (RFC 4648 section 5) of 16 random bytes, no '=' padding, 22 chars.
SAS commitment = SHA-256(UTF8('ReyDesk/sas-commit/v1') || n_c): plain concatenation, NO length prefix (spec 2.2 step 1). n_c and n_h are 32 bytes. Hosts compare with a fixed-time equality.

SAS transcript = LP('ReyDesk/sas/v1') LP(host_spki) LP(client_spki) LP(n_h) LP(n_c); h = SHA-256(transcript); sas_value = (big-endian uint32 of h[0..3]) mod 1000000; sas_digits = sas_value zero-padded to 6 ASCII digits; sas_display = first 3 digits, one ASCII space, last 3 (UI may localize digits).

Pair v2 payload = LP('ReyDesk/pair/v2') LP(method) LP(token) LP(host_spki) LP(client_spki) LP(requester_device_id) LP(host_desk_id) LP(n_h) LP(n_c). method = UTF-8 decimal text of the PairingMethod enum number (e.g. '4' for PAIRING_METHOD_REMOTE_CODE). token = QR token text for LAN_QR/REMOTE_QR, the canonical 6-digit code for REMOTE_CODE, empty otherwise. requester_device_id = DeviceIdentity.device_id string exactly as sent. host_desk_id = canonical host Desk ID when the request travels over a rendezvous pipe (the pipe target), empty on the LAN medium (even if the QR or TXT carried a Desk ID). n_h, n_c = the SAS nonces for SAS methods (LAN_SAS, REMOTE_CODE), empty otherwise. Method 5 (TRUSTED_ATTENDED) is no longer a pair/v2 method: it uses attended_v3 (below).

attended_v3 payload (M5, spec 2.8) = LP('ReyDesk/attended/client/v3') LP(host_spki) LP(client_spki) LP(requester_device_id) LP(host_desk_id) LP(requester_desk_id) LP(n_h) LP(n_c). Desk IDs both empty on LAN, both canonical over a pipe; n_h and n_c exactly 32 bytes. n_h/n_c test values = SHA-256(UTF8('ReyDesk/test-vector/attended/n_h/<i>')) and SHA-256(UTF8('ReyDesk/test-vector/attended/n_c/<i>')). The attended_v3_payload rows (2026-11-05, T18 M2 fix) were computed by two independent implementations (Python stdlib P-256 with RFC 6979, Node/OpenSSL); payloads and hashes agree byte for byte, signatures were produced by Python and verified by Node, and every negative was checked by both.
Rendezvous auth payload = LP('ReyDesk/rendezvous/auth/v1') LP(server_nonce 32 bytes) LP(public_ws_url UTF-8, exact PUBLIC_WS_URL string) LP(spki) LP(desk_id canonical, empty on first registration).
RevokeSelf payload = LP('ReyDesk/rendezvous/revoke/v1') LP(server_nonce), where server_nonce is the ServerHello nonce of the current authenticated connection.
Pair slot code_hash = SHA-256(LP(desk_id canonical) LP(code 6 ASCII digits) LP(salt 16 bytes)).

Signatures: ECDSA P-256 over SHA-256 of the payload, DER (X9.62 Ecdsa-Sig-Value) encoding, NOT IEEE P1363 r||s. Vectors were signed with RFC 6979 deterministic k; implementations need not produce the same bytes (random k is fine) but must verify every signature_checks row to exactly expect_valid. High-S signatures are not rejected.

TURN REST credential (server only): username = '<expiry_unix decimal>:<first 16 lowercase hex chars of the key fingerprint>'; credential = standard base64 (with padding) of HMAC-SHA1(key = UTF-8 TURN_SECRET, msg = UTF-8 username).

Groups: keys (named key pairs referenced by host_key/client_key/key fields), desk_id_from_bits, desk_id_parse, key_id_from_fingerprint, sas, sas_commitment_check, pair_v2_payload, attended_v3_payload, rendezvous_auth_payload, revoke_self_payload, pair_slot_code_hash, remote_code_parse, qr_token, turn_credential, signature_checks. input_codepoints lists the input's Unicode code points so editors cannot silently change them.
